messages.subject: Trapping webs: multipliers and right-truncation
parts:
I have a pair of concerns regarding trapping webs and was hoping someone =
out there could shed some light on the subject. I ran a number of webs =
in a burned ponderosa pine forest on salvage logged and non-logged =
treatments. Peromyscus species comprised the bulk of the captures.

1) Captures consistantly increased with distance from the web's center. =
As a result, the detection functions fit to the data produce denstiy =
estimates lower than what was observed. Right-truncation works to a =
degree, but not without producing very large confidence intervals and =
greater CV values. Left-truncation drives the estimate down further.
Is this a common problem with trapping webs and how is it dealt =
with?

2) Mark-recapture data showed that the g(0)=3D1 assumption was met with =
varying success. That is, I oftern had new individuals appearing on the =
last day of trapping (4 trap nights). The users guide for program =
DISTANCE suggests dividing the density estimate by the observed g(0) in =
these cases. I have ideas on how to calculate a value for g(0), but =
wanted to hear how other people have approached this issue first.

If you have any suggestions, or need more background, please refer to my =
e-mail at:
krwi...@stcloudstat.edu

Thanks for your time!
